LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.pmfChannelKernel: On a countable input space with measurable singletons, a channel W defines a probability kernel by taking the measure of its output distribution W(·|a) at each input a.
The kernel induced by a channel on a countable input space with measurable singletons is a Markov kernel because every row is a probability measure.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.pmfChannelKernel_: At each input a, the measure returned by the channel kernel is precisely the measure associated with the probability distribution W(·|a).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.channelJoint_toMe: On countable input and output spaces with measurable singletons, the measure of the joint input–output law equals the measure obtained by drawing the input from p and then drawing the output from the kernel W.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.channelPosterior: Given prior p on a finite input alphabet, the posterior channel sends each positive-probability output b to the conditional distribution of the input given b. At an impossible output its specified fallback is the input marginal p.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.channelPosterior_: Draw Y by passing p through W, then draw X from the posterior given Y. The resulting law of (Y,X) equals the original input–output joint law with the coordinates exchanged.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.isSufficientChann: For a family of priors pθ on a finite input alphabet, W is sufficient exactly when there is a single reverse channel R whose row at b agrees with the posterior under pθ for every θ and every b of positive probability under the corresponding output law.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.klDiv_channel_eq_: Let W be a channel between finite discrete alphabets, with output laws p′ and q′ for input laws p and q. Then D(p∥q) = D(p′∥q′) + D(J₁∥J₂), allowing infinite values. Both J₁ and J₂ draw the output from p′. Given that output, J₁ draws the input from the posterior for p and J₂ from the posterior for q. At an output of zero probability under its own law, the corresponding posterior defaults to its input law.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.klDiv_channel_le: For a channel W between finite discrete alphabets and any two input laws p and q, the output laws satisfy D(pW∥qW) ≤ D(p∥q). This inequality allows infinite KL divergence.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.klDiv_channel_eq_: Let W be a channel between finite discrete alphabets, and let its input laws satisfy supp(p) ⊆ supp(q). The channel preserves D(p∥q) exactly when the two posterior kernels for the input given the output agree almost everywhere under the output law pW.

Let W be a channel between finite discrete alphabets, and let its input laws satisfy supp(p) ⊆ supp(q). Then D(pW∥qW) = D(p∥q) exactly when the posterior laws of the input under p and q agree at every output of positive probability under pW.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.toReal_klDiv_chan: Under supp(p) ⊆ supp(q), KL divergence on finite discrete alphabets obeys D(pW∥qW) ≤ D(p∥q) as an inequality between finite real quantities.

Let W be a channel between finite discrete alphabets. If supp(p) ⊆ supp(q), the input and output KL divergences are finite. Their real values D(p∥q) and D(pW∥qW) are equal exactly when the posterior laws of the input under p and q agree at every output in the support of pW.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.klDiv_map_le: Let f map one finite discrete alphabet to another. Applying f to two laws p and q on its domain gives output laws whose KL divergence is at most D(p∥q), allowing infinite divergence.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.toReal_klDiv_map_: If supp(p) ⊆ supp(q), the real KL divergence between their pushforwards under any map between finite discrete alphabets is at most D(p∥q).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.klDiv_channelComp: For channels W followed by V with finite discrete intermediate and final alphabets, D((pW)V∥(qW)V) ≤ D(pW∥qW) for all input laws p and q, allowing infinite values.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.klDiv_channel_cas: In a cascade W then V with finite discrete intermediate and output alphabets, extended KL divergence between two output laws after both channels is at most their divergence after W alone.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.toReal_klDiv_chan: Given supp(p) ⊆ supp(q) and finite discrete intermediate and final alphabets, the real KL divergence after W followed by V is at most the real divergence after W.
If supp(p) ⊆ supp(q), adding a second channel V to W with finite discrete intermediate and output alphabets gives the real inequality D((pW)V∥(qW)V) ≤ D(pW∥qW).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.klDiv_channel_inv: On a finite discrete alphabet, if r is stationary for W, meaning rW = r, then D(pW∥r) ≤ D(p∥r) for every p, as an extended-real inequality.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.toReal_klDiv_chan: On a finite discrete alphabet, if rW = r and supp(p) ⊆ supp(r), the finite real divergence to r cannot increase after W, so D(pW∥r) ≤ D(p∥r).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_le_entrop: If W preserves the uniform distribution on a finite nonempty alphabet, applying W to any input distribution p gives H(p) ≤ H(pW).
For a channel on a finite nonempty alphabet whose every column sums to one, output entropy is at least input entropy, H(pW) ≥ H(p).
